title: PA-04: Adults meeting muscle-strengthening activity guideline
method: NHIS; adults 18+; age-adjusted to 2000 standard population
limitation: Leisure-time self-report. Do not multiply age-adjusted percentages by current population to obtain counts.

title: PA-02: Adults meeting aerobic physical activity guideline
method: NHIS; adults 18+; age-adjusted to 2000 standard population
limitation: Behavioral threshold, not purchase intent.

title: PA-05: Adults meeting aerobic and muscle-strengthening activity guidelines
method: NHIS; adults 18+; age-adjusted to 2000 standard population
limitation: The complement includes anyone missing either guideline; not all are completely inactive.

title: Leisure-Time Physical Activity Among Women of Reproductive Age — United States, 2022 and 2024
method: NHIS women 18–44; Table 1 gives unweighted n=10,891 and weighted n=56,087,223
limitation: Abstract says 10,981, conflicting with tables and table footnote. Use table-specific estimates. Table 2 reports strength sufficiency 31.1%; adding rounded Table 1 categories yields 31.2%. Do not replace direct published estimates with rounded sums.

title: Erratum: Vol. 74, No. 41
method: Corrected abstract category labels
limitation: Read with source 4; no new sample.

title: Americans Plan to Invest $60 Billion in Health and Fitness in 2026
method: Online sample of 2,000 U.S. adults; publisher describes as nationally representative
limitation: Seasonal stated intention; exact subgroup base and joint response covariance not published. Claimed overall margin of error does not establish a significant 50% vs 48% subgroup difference.

title: 81 Million Americans Were Members of a Fitness Facility in 2025, New HFA Report Finds
method: Annual national study of approximately 18,000 U.S. residents age 6+
limitation: Different age base and questionnaire from NHIS. Membership association with activity is not causal. Public release only; complete report not purchased.

title: How 77 Million Fitness Members Work Out
method: Rolling 12-month participation; U.S. population age 6+
limitation: Training participation is not unmet demand. Lower frequency may have multiple explanations; do not infer affordability caused it.

title: Motivators and Barriers to Engaging in Brain-Healthy Behaviors: Adults Ages 50-Plus
method: Nationally representative online and telephone survey of 1,009 adults 50+
limitation: Accessible indexed publisher text; direct page fetch returned 403. Broad behavior questions do not measure willingness to buy exercise instruction.

title: Benefits of Physical Activity and Exercise: A Survey on Healthy Living Among Adults Ages 50 and Older
method: NORC Foresight 50+ panel; 1,948 U.S. adults; weighted to CPS
limitation: Older corroborating evidence; its exercise questions should not be equated with NHIS guideline classification.

title: The $2 trillion global wellness market gets a millennial and Gen Z glow-up
method: More than 9,000 respondents across China, Germany, UK and U.S.; only explicitly U.S. figures used
limitation: Public article does not document a probability sampling frame. Broad wellness spending is not a digital-fitness TAM.

title: The trends defining the $1.8 trillion global wellness market in 2024
data_period: 2024 report; earlier survey cited for 37% figure
method: Multi-country wellness consumer research; page 11 discusses sleep unmet needs
limitation: Historical, broad wellness claim. The cited 37% came from an earlier report; do not label it a new 2024 or 2026 measure.

title: Short Sleep Duration and Sleep Difficulties Among Adults: United States, 2024
method: NHIS civilian noninstitutionalized adults; crude estimates; survey confidence intervals
limitation: Short sleep, insomnia, tiredness, and dissatisfied customers are different categories.

title: Chronic Pain and High-impact Chronic Pain in U.S. Adults, 2023
publisher: Lucas and Sohi, NCHS Data Brief 518
method: NHIS civilian noninstitutionalized adults; crude estimates
limitation: Chronic pain is not synonymous with a mobility-training need or suitability for unsupervised exercise.

title: In U.S., GLP-1 Usage Reaches New High
method: Probability-based Gallup Panel; web survey; n=5,065
limitation: 11% is current use for weight loss, not all indications and not coaching demand. Use revised article, not earlier reposts.

title: KFF Health Tracking Poll: Prescription Drug Costs, Views on Trump Administration Actions, and GLP-1 Use
method: National U.S. adult health tracking poll
limitation: 12% current use includes weight loss or chronic conditions; not directly comparable to Gallup's weight-loss-specific question.

title: Noom Launches Free Version of Its Powerful GLP-1 Companion
method: Vendor launch announcement; free companion, nutrition tools and workouts
limitation: Feature and price-position evidence only; efficacy and body-composition claims not independently evaluated.

title: GLP-1 Success Program
method: Vendor program page
limitation: Confirms existing nutrition and strength support; not independently verified efficacy.

title: Ladder: Your Daily Workout Plan
method: Vendor feature and positioning page
limitation: Already offers strength, home and gym plans, demonstrations, coaching and tracking. Feature presence does not establish universal satisfaction.

title: Caliber Workout App
method: Vendor feature page
limitation: Markets free tracker; feature-by-feature entitlement not audited. No coaching price inferred.

title: Train With Meg
method: Creator's program page
limitation: Before the Barbell is advertised as free eight-week beginner program. No independent outcome claim.

title: SilverSneakers Member Value Flyer
method: Vendor benefit description
limitation: Included in selected Medicare plans; not universally free to every older adult.

title: Future Pro coach matching
method: Vendor purchase-entry page
limitation: Lists $199 regular and $50 first-month promotion at access; promotions may change. No checkout or purchase performed.

title: Sleepio suitability
method: Vendor product and suitability description
limitation: Digital sleep improvement already exists. Clinical suitability and access require separate assessment.

title: Americans Cite Cost of Heathy Food as Biggest Barrier to a Heart-Healthy Diet
method: National survey described by publisher
limitation: Historical perceived barriers, not an objective food-price comparison or app demand measure.

title: Megastudies improve the impact of applied behavioural science
method: Randomized four-week digital interventions among 61,293 U.S. chain gym members
limitation: Causal evidence in enrolled gym members; neither nationwide demand nor proof of sustained results for the proposed product.

title: Virtual Physical Therapy and Personalized Pain Care
method: Vendor service page
limitation: Clinical competition and delivery model; no market-share or effectiveness calculation.

title: ABC Trainerize features
method: Vendor product page
limitation: Coach operations, habits and AI generation already supplied; vendor user counts not used to size unmet demand.

title: State of Subscription Apps 2026
method: Transaction-based vendor dataset across subscription apps
limitation: Selected global platform customers, not all fitness apps or all consumers. Retention and conversion definitions vary; do not equate initial renewal with year-one retention.

title: Time To Flex: Bridging The Protein Knowledge Action Gap
method: Publisher synthesis of 2025 food and protein surveys
limitation: Protein interest is not protein deficiency, unmet service demand, or willingness to buy a macro calculator.

title: 2025 IFIC Food & Health Survey: Full Report
method: Dynata online consumer panel; n=3,000 ages 18–80; weighted to 2024 CPS
limitation: Weighted online panel; 2026 ingredient-safety release does not supersede every 2025 nutrition measure.

title: Aerobic Physical Activity Among Adults Age 18 and Older: United States, 2024
publisher: Elgaddal and Kramarow, NCHS Data Brief 555
method: NHIS; crude adult estimates and published confidence intervals
limitation: 47.2% crude is distinct from Healthy People's 48.0% age-adjusted rate.

title: HFA Resolution Survey / public trust comparison
data_period: December 2025 public survey and February 2026 policymaker survey
method: Publisher comparison of two surveys; public figure explicitly isolated
limitation: Perceived cancellation difficulty is a trust issue; not evidence of demand for another subscription.

title: Half of Americans Want to Lose Weight
method: U.S. adult Health and Healthcare Survey; Gallup Poll Social Series
limitation: Wanting to lose weight and seriously trying are distinct questions. Neither measures dissatisfaction or willingness to buy a fitness product.

title: Prevalence of Overweight, Obesity, and Severe Obesity Among Adults Age 20 and Older: United States, 1960–1962 Through August 2021–August 2023
publisher: Fryar, Afful and Saif, NCHS Health E-Stat 111
method: NHANES stratified multistage probability sample; measured height and weight; adults 20+; excludes pregnancy and missing measurements
limitation: 40.3% is both the rounded crude and age-adjusted obesity estimate; ledger records crude. BMI classification is not dissatisfaction or product suitability.

title: How the Weight Watchers Program Works: Find Your Plan
method: Vendor program page
limitation: Confirms food, activity, support, and clinical offerings; not an independent effectiveness or market-share estimate.
